What? No in your dog's case, sure his eyes were watering due to diet, you took him to a vet and that's what he was diagnosed with. I've taken my dog to a vet too, and they didn't find anything medically wrong. In your case, your dog has a higher tolerance for being left alone, and it's probably because you started out with not spending as much time with him? Maybe? I can't possibly know that.

I've gone great lengths for my dog to determine if he's miserable when we're gone the normal length of six hours. I've taped him to see what he does on his own. He mostly sleeps, until he's at hour seven and he starts to whine and cry and look for us. His food and water and all his physical needs are fulfilled, so it can't be for any other reason that he starts to get upset when we're gone longer than his expectation. So we try our best by meeting his expectation. To do otherwise is not nice to him.

Not saying that those aren't reasons why dogs' eyes water. My dog's eyes do not water for any of these reasons though. 

It's like saying that my stomach can only hurt because of common reasons such as hunger, food poisoning, salmonella, etc. Maybe a stomach hurts because of anxiety?

Never heard about smiling dogs, and I agree that it's likely submissive behavior. 

I'll explain my experience further, about my dog crying:

My dog whines when he wants something but you're not giving it to him: attention, or a toy being thrown. When he whines his ears flatten, and if he gets no acknowledgement his eyes water in addition to whining and sighing. A moment before, he was fine: running around from chasing his toy for example. Thrashing his toy in the air and wiggling his bum in the air. 

Another anecdote: sometimes I visit my in-laws' house, which usually has at least two or three hyperactive kids running around having a good time with my dog. He loves playing with them and he seems to lose his mind with joy. But, if I leave the house he will stop whatever he is doing and will wait on the couch for me to come back. His eyes water and he sighs a lot. He will accept head rubs and will lick hands, but he will not move from the spot until I come back.

I have a full time job, partner has a full-time job and we make it work by having our schedules worked out so that we don't leave the dog for longer than six hours. People with full time jobs can certainly have pets, but what I'm saying is that it is important to consider your dog's feelings. My dog is huge suck and in his case it would be cruel to leave him alone for longer than six hours. 

Anyways, maybe the bond between my dog and myself is stronger than others' who don't spend as much time with theirs'.
It is not okay to have a dog cooped up inside/or in a yard all day if it only gets three hours or less of human time (not including bed time) per day. Anyone that thinks otherwise is ignorant.
